name: staq
why: Quantum circuit toolkit from a research paper; an obscure real-science corner worth a look if you want to see how quantum compilers work.

brief.what_it_is: staq is a C++ library and command-line tool suite for synthesizing, transforming, optimizing and compiling quantum circuits. It takes OpenQASM 2.0 circuit source as its main input and can be used either through its binary tools (staq, staq_mapper, staq_resource_estimator and others) or as a header-only C++ library for parsing and manipulating OpenQASM 2.0. Output is transformed or translated circuit code, such as other circuit languages or libraries. A Python 3 wrapper, pystaq, is also included.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames staq as a modern, low-dependency C++17 alternative for quantum circuit compilation work, and says it is inspired by Clang. Its stated goal is source-to-source transformation of OpenQASM 2.0 without losing the original source structure.
brief.how_it_works: Unlike most compilers, staq does not lower circuits into an intermediate representation. It manipulates the OpenQASM 2.0 syntax tree directly, so circuits can be inspected and transformed (in most cases) while keeping the original source layout. The README says this makes translation to other circuit languages easier to follow against the original source. Logic synthesis is delegated to the EPFL logic synthesis libraries, and the OpenQASM 2.0 parser was adapted from Bruno Schmitt's tweedledum.

brief.install_notes: Requires CMake and a C++17 compiler (GCC, Clang or MSVC). GNU MP is optional but needed to build the grid synth tools staq_grid_synth and staq_qasm_synth; if CMake cannot find it, those tools are skipped. On Windows the README recommends installing GNU MP and pkgconf through vcpkg, then passing the vcpkg toolchain file to CMake. Installing sources puts headers in /usr/local/include/staq on UNIX or C:\Program Files (x86)\staq on Windows. No accounts or hardware are needed.
brief.standout: The Clang-inspired design keeps the OpenQASM 2.0 syntax tree itself as the working representation, so a circuit can be edited in place and still look like the source you started with. That is unusual compared with IR-based compiler toolkits.
brief.status: quiet. The README is headed Version 3.5, dated 8 March 2024, and its copyright runs to 2025. It has a GitHub Actions build badge. I could not see commit dates or release history, so this is tentative.
brief.caveats: The homepage, a Wiley/IOP paper PDF, was blocked by a bot-protection captcha, so I could not read the paper. Only OpenQASM 2.0 is named as the input language. Grid synth tools need GNU MP and are skipped without it. Windows setup is more involved and uses vcpkg. The brew caveats field is empty. The software is MIT licensed.
quotes: staq is a modern C++ library for the synthesis, transformation, optimization and compilation of quantum circuits.
Inspired by Clang, staq is designed to manipulate OpenQASM 2.0 syntax trees directly, rather than through an intermediate representation which makes retrieving the original source code impossible.
This makes staq ideally suited for source-to-source transformations, where only specific changes are desired.
